history.summary: Mi Casa (2012, 457 units, 99yr from 2008) 1,259 sqft 3BR asking $1.60M / $1,271 psf, ~400m from Choa Chu Kang NS4 MRT/bus interchange. A genuinely liquid, well-proven OCR family condo — 744 transactions, 313 resales, 95.5% sold at a profit — and the cheapest of six live 3BR asks. But the algo's 780 rests on a '-16.3% vs age-adjusted D23 median' reading that is a district artifact: D23 is two price worlds, and on the Choa Chu Kang side Mi Casa is the MOST expensive project (2025-26 resale median $1,326 psf vs The Warren $1,186, Northvale $1,102, Regent Grove $1,003). Against its own size band's trailing prints the discount is only ~3-4%, into a tape that has flattened (URA 2025 median $1,333 psf -> 2026 YTD $1,288; PropertyGuru 6-mo avg $1,253 vs 12-mo $1,267). Fair entry, no edge.
history.rating_rationale: Priced at fair value, not cheap, once the comp set is its own sub-market. The 1,150-1,400 sqft resale prints at Mi Casa over the last 12 months run $1,246-$1,346 psf (median ~$1,333); $1,271 psf is ~3-4% under that mid-point, and the 2026 prints plus the softening 6-month average say the market is drifting down to meet the ask rather than the ask undercutting the market. That thin gap is fully explainable by an unverified floor — the two cheapest 2026 prints ($1,246 and $1,288 psf) were both floors 1-5, and PropertyGuru serves no floor_level or facing for this listing. Carry is weak (3.15% gross / 1.87% net on a $4,200 URA-contract rent, 20 contracts), so a 5-7yr return is almost entirely appreciation-dependent — and the appreciation case is the weakest part: the project already re-rated +31% from a 2022 median of $1,021 psf to $1,333 in 2025, momentum is negative, and the JRL catalyst that carried that re-rating slipped to mid-2028 (announced Mar 2026) and has no measured forward power in our own backtest. What holds the rating up rather than down: nothing here is broken. 83 years of lease, deep buyer pool (457 units, 71% historically HDB upgraders, $1.6M sits in the deepest quantum band), and a 313-resale book at 95.5% profitable is real downside evidence. A Buy needs either a confirmed mid/high floor at this price or a negotiated ~$1.50-1.55M; at $1.60M sight-unseen it is a Neutral.
red_flags: score_1000 780 is artifact-inflated: the largest MMR component is age_value 12.17, driven by -16.3% vs the age-adjusted D23 median ($1,518) — but D23 is bifurcated. Hillview/Dairy Farm stock trades $1,531-$1,986 psf; the Choa Chu Kang cohort trades $1,003-$1,326. Mi Casa is the TOP of its own sub-market, not a discount to it.
Gross yield 3.15% / net 1.87% — thin carry for OCR; the whole 5-7yr case rides on price appreciation.

Already re-rated: project median psf +31% 2022 ($1,021) -> 2025 ($1,333). 2026 YTD prints median $1,288 (n=3) and PropertyGuru's 6-month average ($1,253) sits below its 12-month average ($1,267) — a flattening-to-softening tape.

Floor and facing unknown — PropertyGuru serves neither for this listing, and no profiles/ entry exists for Mi Casa. The 2026 prints below $1,300 psf were all floors 1-5, so the modest discount may simply be a low-floor unit at fair value.

The 'price dropped' badge is partly a unit_group chaining artifact: history spans three listing ids (relisted_from 500180521) and the $1,332.79 psf entry implies 1,238 sqft — a different unit. The $1.688M -> $1.60M path for this 1,259 sqft unit is plausible but not verifiable to one agent/id.
Six live 3BR asks in the same size band ($1,271-$1,350 psf), several with cuts — the same crowd will be competing at exit.
JRL first stage delayed to mid-2028 (from end-2027), announced 5 Mar 2026 — the catalyst is later than the 2027 story that priced the last leg.
catalysts: ~380-400m to Choa Chu Kang NS4 MRT + bus interchange, which becomes a JRL interchange — genuine transit quality, though largely already in the price.
OCR — the strongest measured forward region in our panel (realized fwd +3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1%, CCR +1.9%).
$1.60M sits in the deepest HDB-upgrader quantum band; realsmart records 71% HDB buyers and 82% sold at launch — the natural buyer pool for the exit is the one that already bought here.
Newest and closest-to-MRT project on the Choa Chu Kang side (2012 vs Regent Grove/Northvale/Palm Gardens 1990s-2000s) — a durable relative-quality position within its sub-market.

history.summary: A 1,281 sqft Mi Casa unit marketed as 4BR at $1,729,999 / $1,351 psf. Mi Casa's developer unit mix puts 4-bedrooms at 1,384-2,316 sqft, so this size cannot be one — and the identical unit (same price, sqft, 3 baths, same address) is simultaneously listed as a 3BR. The ask sits above the project's ENTIRE trailing-12-month transacted range ($1,129-$1,346 psf) and +4.9% over the April-2026 URA print for this exact 1,281 sqft size ($1,288 psf), with four cheaper same-size asks live in the same project today. Good development, wrong unit, wrong price.
history.rating_rationale:
Avoid on the LISTING, not on the development. Mi Casa itself is a proven, liquid OCR family condo — 745 transactions, 313 resales, 95.5% sold at a profit, 342m from Choa Chu Kang NS4/BP1 (a JRL JS1 interchange from mid-2028), 81 years of lease left. The problem is this specific unit at this specific price.

(1) The bedroom count is almost certainly wrong. Mi Casa's developer mix runs 2BR 1,020-1,292 sqft, 3BR 1,260-2,217 sqft, 4BR 1,384-2,316 sqft — 1,281 sqft is BELOW the smallest 4BR and at the bottom of the 3BR range. The same unit is posted twice, once as 4BR (id 500218596) and once as 3BR (id 500218589), at an identical $1,729,999 / 1,281 sqft / 3 baths / 323 Choa Chu Kang Ave 3. bed_bands returns 'ok' for both because URA rental filings in the 1250-1350 band include 46 contracts self-declared 4BR — landlords file a convertible study as a bedroom; the developer's mix is the stronger authority. At exit this transacts and is recorded as a 3BR, into the 3BR buyer pool.

(2) The ask is above the project's whole recent print range. This exact 1,281 sqft size printed $1,288 psf ($1.65M) in Apr-2026, $1,225 in May-2025, $1,304 in Sep-2024 and $1,366 in Dec-2024. EdgeProp's trailing-12-month band for the project is $1,129-$1,346 psf (avg $1,263); the freshest print of any size is 30-Jul-2026 at $1,286 psf. At $1,351 psf this ask clears the top of all of it — before negotiation, and with floor and condition unverified (PropertyGuru serves neither). Fair value for this size is ~$1.65M; the ask is ~$80k above it.

(3) The 770 score is artifact-inflated and label-sensitive. Its largest component is age_value 8.52, from '-11% vs the age-adjusted D23 median of $1,518'. D23 is two price worlds: on my own 2025+ resale read of the district, Hillview/Dairy Farm/Bukit Batok stock runs $1,465-$1,919 psf (Midwood $1,919, Dairy Farm Residences $1,830, Le Quest $1,634), while the Choa Chu Kang cluster runs Mi Casa $1,288 > The Warren $1,182 > Northvale $1,103 > Palm Gardens $1,062 > Regent Grove $1,010. Mi Casa is the MOST expensive project in its own sub-market, 5th cheapest of 48 in the district — the gap to the D23 median is a permanent location level, not value. The algo's own project-relative measure agrees: psf_value is NEGATIVE (-1.65) and psf_premium_vs_ura_median_pct is +2.7%. Note also that the identical unit scores 770 as a '4BR' and 741 as a '3BR' — 29 points of pure label noise.

(4) Carry is thin and the local tape has stopped rising. 3.33% gross / 1.86% net on a $4,800 rent (11 URA contracts; realsmart's independent estimate is 3.4%). The project's annual median PSF went $1,233 (2024) -> $1,310 (2025) -> $1,273 (2026 YTD, 6 sales), so the whole 5-7yr case rides on appreciation from an above-range entry. Ten other Mi Casa asks are live right now, four of them cheaper per psf at 1,238-1,270 sqft ($1,271 / $1,284 / $1,301 / $1,329) — the buyer has strictly better options inside the same project, and the same crowd will be competing at exit.

What would change the call: this unit at ~$1.62-1.65M ($1,265-$1,288 psf) is a Neutral — a fair entry into a genuinely liquid OCR development with a real transit catalyst. The July-2026 eval rated the $1.60M / $1,271 psf 3BR exactly that. Paying 6% more for the same thing with a disputed bed count is not.

Confidence medium rather than high: the pricing and unit-mix evidence is verifiable and decisive, but floor level and renovation state are unknown for this unit, and a genuinely renovated high-floor unit would narrow (not close) the gap to the project's $1,346 ceiling.
red_flags: BED COUNT DISPUTED — marketed as 4BR at 1,281 sqft, but Mi Casa's developer unit mix starts 4BR at 1,384 sqft (3BR: 1,260-2,217 sqft). The identical unit ($1,729,999 / 1,281 sqft / 3 baths / 323 CCK Ave 3) is concurrently listed as a 3BR under id 500218589. Treat as a 3BR, or a 3+study, until a floor plan proves otherwise.

OVERPRICED VS THE PROJECT'S OWN PRINTS — $1,351 psf is above the entire trailing-12-month transacted range ($1,129-$1,346 psf, avg $1,263 per EdgeProp) and +4.9% over the Apr-2026 URA print for this exact 1,281 sqft size ($1,650,000 / $1,288 psf). Freshest print of any size: 30-Jul-2026 at $1,286 psf.

score_1000 770 is a D23-bifurcation artifact — age_value 8.52 rests on '-11% vs age-adjusted D23 median $1,518', but that median is set by Hillview/Dairy Farm stock ($1,465-$1,919). Mi Casa ($1,288 median, 2025+ resales) is the TOP of the Choa Chu Kang cluster (The Warren $1,182, Northvale $1,103, Palm Gardens $1,062, Regent Grove $1,010), not a discount to it. The algo's project-relative psf_value is negative (-1.65).

Score is label-sensitive noise: the same unit scores 770 as '4BR' and 741 as '3BR'. The 29-point gap that pulled this listing through the weekly gate is a data-entry difference, not a property difference.
Thin carry — 3.33% gross / 1.86% net yield (rent $4,800, 11 URA contracts; realsmart's independent estimate 3.4%). The entire 5-7yr case depends on appreciation.
Local tape has flattened: project annual median PSF $1,233 (2024) -> $1,310 (2025) -> $1,273 (2026 YTD, 6 sales). Already re-rated +39.7% since 2019 (realsmart).
Ten competing live asks in the same project, four cheaper per psf at similar size ($1,271-$1,329 for 1,238-1,270 sqft). Same competition at exit.
Floor level and facing unknown (PropertyGuru serves neither; no profiles/ entry for Mi Casa). Notably, three of the four recorded 1,281 sqft prints were floors 01-05, so this size may skew low-floor.

JRL Stage 1 slipped to mid-2028 from late-2027 (announced 4 Mar 2026) — the catalyst is later than the story that priced the last leg, and our panel measures no forward power in future-infrastructure scores anyway.

Newest and closest-to-MRT project on the Choa Chu Kang side (2012 vs Regent Grove / Northvale / Palm Gardens, 1990s-2000s) — a durable relative-quality position within its sub-market.

agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The 5.22%/yr ura_5yr_cagr (66 txns) is trailing and should not be carried forward: it is measured off a 2021 base ($948 psf median) through the post-COVID OCR re-rating, and the project's own tape has since flattened — annual median PSF $1,233 (2024) -> $1,310 (2025) -> $1,273 (2026 YTD). Our panel measures ~0 forward power in trailing CAGR. I override to 3.2%/yr: at or just below the realized OCR regional mean (+3.7%), marked down because Mi Casa already sits at the ceiling of its own Choa Chu Kang sub-market (the next-priciest CCK-side project, The Warren, is 8% cheaper) so it has less room to re-rate than the district figure implies. Separately, the entry matters more than the rate here: buying ~5% above the last 12 months' print range means the first ~1.5 years of that 3.2% only recovers the overpay. realsmart's 95.5%-profitable record (299 of 313 resales) is real downside evidence but is backward-looking — it is measured on 2009-2012 launch entries into a market that has since re-rated ~40%, and says nothing about a 2026 buyer entering above the project's recent range.
